prior_art.basis: Independent review by claude-independent-prior-art-reviewer-20261106: No humanoid robot does any household chore autonomously, so the Main KPI of 1,000,000,000 home humanoid robots is unmet. The leading consumer home humanoid, 1X NEO, opened $20,000 preorders in October 2025 for 2026 delivery, deliveries were not confirmed by August 2026, and most demonstrated tasks were teleoperated by a remote human in VR (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1X_Technologies). Open foundation models exist and are the state of the art: NVIDIA GR00T N1 for humanoids (https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2503.14734), OpenVLA (https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2406.09246) and pi-0.5, which reports partial open-world generalisation to cleaning tasks in unseen homes (https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2504.16054); benchmarks such as RoboCasa365 (https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2603.04356) measure task suites, not any chore. Open GitHub humanoid household projects are small simulations (HANDY, 8 stars). Class neutral, as for the comparable home-robot project OPP-07921: benefit to households and carers, but labour displacement and in-home privacy risk from teleoperation. Honest limit: running or fine-tuning the open VLA models on household benchmarks is a known baseline; new work is reliable long-horizon autonomy across arbitrary chores without teleoperation, with verified safety around people.
